newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich places $1 billion in securities.
newsitem.headline: Zurich places $1 billion in securities.

text.p: Zurich Group said it had successfully placed $1 billion in 40-year capital securities with proceeds to be used to finance corporate development, including potential acquisitions.

The securities, issued by a specially created U.S. unit called Zurich Capital Trust I, carry an annual coupon of 8.376 percent payable semi-annually in arrears starting December 1, 1997, it said in a statement.
"Proceeds of the offering will be used for general business purposes, including the funding of any potential acquisitions of the group," it added.
"For the Zurich Group, this financial transaction presents a welcome opportunity to obtain long-term financing at an attractive after-tax rate without diluting shareholder capital," it said.
The private placement was managed by Goldman, Sachs & Co, Credit Suisse First Boston, J.P. Morgan & Co, Morgan Stanley & Co and UBS Securities.
Company officials were not immediately available for additional comment.
According to unconfirmed press reports, Zurich is in talks to acquire private U.S. money management company Scudder, Stevens & Clark for around $1.5 billion.
